name: Atlantis The Royal
positioning: Large-scale beachfront resort on the crescent of the Palm Jumeirah, designed around light, space and pools in the sky
best_for: Travelers who want suites and penthouses with their own private pools
Families who want a kids' club, a family pool and included access to the Aquaventure waterpark
Guests who want a lively resort with sky-high pools and fire-and-water shows

facts.text: The resort is situated on the crescent of the Palm Jumeirah.
The hotel was designed by the architects behind New York's One Vanderbilt.
The design moves away from the underwater Lost City theme of Atlantis The Palm, replacing it with light, space and pools in the sky.
The Signature Penthouses are individually designed, with private pools and panoramic infinity views.
Suites have open terraces and private pools.
Guest rooms have views across the Palm and the ocean.
Room bathrooms are separated from the bedroom by glass walls that become opaque at the touch of a 'magic glass' button.
Royal Club guests have access to the Royal Club Lounge.
Spa facilities include a salt cave, a hydrotherapy pool, aromatherapy, chromotherapy and a charcoal sauna.
The resort shares a 1.2-mile beach with neighboring Atlantis The Palm.
For children there is the Atlantis Explorers' Club, a children's splash pad and family watersports, and the Royal Pool is the family pool.
The resort's restaurants and bars range from celebrity chef concepts to Emirati afternoon tea.

highlights.text: Forty-four of the suites and penthouses have their own glass-sided pools high up in the air.
Cloud 22 is a swimming pool perched high on top of the skybridge.
The Skyblaze Fountain, a fire-and-water performance at the heart of the resort, rises 28 metres into the air.
The spa's 'local list' treatments feature ingredients like oud, dates, Dubai desert sand and Gulf sea salt.
All stays include complimentary access to the adjacent Aquaventure waterpark and aquarium.

considerations.text: The beach can have jellyfish at certain times of year, signalled by purple warning flags, so the pools are the safer swim then.
WhataHotel notes the high-energy resort atmosphere may not suit guests seeking a tranquil retreat.
WhataHotel notes ultra-premium pricing that reflects the luxury positioning.
